content.title: About
content.content: Dry barley cereal for toddlers (Baby Toddler cereal, barley, dry) is designed for children from 6 months old. The cereal is made from whole barley that has been heat‑treated, without added sugar, salt, or artificial flavors. It dissolves easily in warm water or milk, creating a smooth, easily digestible porridge.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Barley is one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown for over 10,000 years.
Dry infant cereals are convenient to store and transport and do not require refrigeration.
Barley contains beta‑glucans, which support the immune system.
The product is processed to keep gluten levels within safe limits for young children.
Only whole‑grain material is used, with no additives, making it hypoallergenic.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps develop a balanced gut microbiome in toddlers.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Barley provides thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, which are essential for energy metabolism and nervous system development.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron is necessary for hemoglobin formation and maintaining energy levels in children.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The absence of added sugar helps establish healthy taste preferences early on.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Beta‑glucans in barley stimulate immune cells, aiding protection against infections.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some children may be allergic to barley; monitor for reactions when first introduced.

items.title: Gluten sensitivity
items.content: Although gluten content is low, children with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should avoid it.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: The dry product must be prepared to a smooth consistency; large particles can pose a choking risk for toddlers.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Mix 150 ml of warm (not hot) water or milk with the cereal, stir thoroughly, and let it sit for 2–3 minutes. Add more liquid if needed to reach the desired texture. The porridge can be enriched with fruit or vegetable puree.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. After opening, use within 30 days. Discard if any off‑odor, mold, or discoloration appears.

burrito-with-beans-and-rice-cheese.title: Burrito with Beans, Rice, and Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A burrito is a Mexican dish consisting of a large soft tortilla wrapped around a filling of beans, rice, cheese, and often additional ingredients such as vegetables, meat, or sauces. The beans‑rice‑cheese version is popular among vegetarians and anyone looking for a hearty, easy‑to‑prepare meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tortilla for a burrito is traditionally made from corn or wheat flour; wheat tortillas are softer and more common in the United States.
Beans used are usually black or pinto, both rich in protein and fiber.
Mexican rice is often cooked with tomato sauce and spices, giving it a characteristic color and flavor.
Cheese commonly added is cheddar, Monterey Jack, or Mexican “queso” that melts and binds the other ingredients.
Burritos are frequently served with salsa, guacamole, sour cream, or a squeeze of lime for extra zest.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Beans and cheese provide a substantial amount of protein needed for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Beans and rice supply fiber that supports healthy digestion and helps keep you feeling full.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice offers slowly released energy, which helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D from cheese
items.content: Cheese is a good source of calcium for bone health and contains vitamin D that aids calcium absorption.

items.title: Contains beneficial micronutrients
items.content: Beans provide iron, magnesium, and folate, while rice contributes vitamin B6 and thiamine, supporting metabolism.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: A cheese‑and‑rice burrito can be calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Cheese and prepared sauces often contain a lot of salt; people with hypertension should opt for low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese contains lactose, so those who are lactose‑intolerant may need dairy‑free alternatives.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to beans and should substitute another protein source.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Burritos can be enjoyed hot or at room temperature. Hold it in your hand, cut it in half if desired, and add fresh veggies, salsa, guacamole, or sour cream to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, wrap tightly in plastic wrap and freeze up to 2 months, then reheat in the microwave or oven.

carrots-frozen-cooked-no-added-fat.title: Carrots, frozen, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen, cooked carrots with no added fat are pre‑steamed or boiled carrot pieces that are quickly frozen to preserve flavor, color, and nutrients. The product is ready to eat after reheating and can be used as a side dish, in soups, stews, or salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carrots are one of the most widely cultivated vegetables, grown in over 100 countries.
Freezing retains up to 90 % of beta‑carotene and vitamin A, which give carrots their bright orange hue.
Fat‑free cooked carrots are popular in diet plans and weight‑loss programs.
Unlike fresh carrots, frozen carrots can be stored for up to 12 months when kept properly.
Quick preparation (usually 3–5 minutes in the microwave) makes them convenient for busy lifestyles.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of frozen carrots contain about 35 kcal, making them an excellent choice for weight management.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium assists in fluid balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: In addition to beta‑carotene, carrots provide vitamin C and other antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to carrots, manifested as skin rashes or swelling.

items.title: Nitrate content
items.content: Carrots can accumulate nitrates; it is advisable not to exceed recommended daily intake, especially for children.

items.title: Texture loss with prolonged storage
items.content: After long freezer storage, carrots may become soft upon thawing, limiting their use in dishes that require crisp texture.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat carrots in the microwave, steamer, or a saucepan with a little water (no added oil). Serve as a side, add to soups, stews, vegetable mixes, or salads. They are also suitable for baby foods as a soft, easily digestible vegetable puree.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen carrots in a sealed bag or container at –18 °C or lower. Once opened, use within 3–4 months. Do not thaw and refreeze to avoid quality loss.

content.title: About
content.content: Chiles rellenos is a classic Mexican dish consisting of large, mild peppers (often poblano) that are stuffed with cheese (sometimes combined with meat or vegetables) and then baked or fried. The cheese melts inside, giving the dish a creamy, rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: "Rellenos" comes from the Spanish verb "rellenar" meaning “to fill.”
Traditional recipes use poblano peppers, but other sweet peppers can be used.
The dish originated in the colonial era after the Spanish introduced cheese to Mexico.
Fillings vary widely—from simple mozzarella to blends of cheese, ham, rice, and spices.
Chiles rellenos are often served with a tomato‑chili sauce or a simple salsa.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheese provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Protein
items.content: When meat or beans are added, the dish becomes a good source of complete protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheese and meat supply B2, B12, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Vitamin C from the pepper
items.content: Sweet peppers are rich in vitamin C, which boosts immunity and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Peppers contain carotenoids and other phytochemicals with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to dairy products.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Many cheeses are salty; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt varieties.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish can be high in calories due to cheese and cooking oil.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Remove seeds from the peppers, stuff them with grated cheese (optionally mixed with meat, rice or veggies), then bake at 180 °C for 20‑25 minutes or pan‑fry until golden. Serve hot, drizzled with tomato sauce, alongside rice, beans, or a fresh salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked chiles rellenos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. They can also be frozen in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.

content.title: About
content.content: Coffee is a beverage made from roasted and ground seeds of the coffee plant. This version is already pre‑light roasted and sweetened with sugar, ready for consumption without any further preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Light roasting preserves more acidity and fruity notes than dark roasting.
Sweetening with sugar is common in ready‑to‑drink coffee products to provide instant sweetness.
Coffee is cultivated in over 70 countries, with Brazil, Vietnam and Colombia being the largest producers.
Sugar helps stabilize flavor during storage of the ready‑made product.
Coffee contains more than 1,000 aromatic compounds.

items.title: Energizing effect
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, increasing alertness and concentration.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Coffee is rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Caffeine can boost metabolic rate and aid fat oxidation.

items.title: Reduced risk of certain diseases
items.content: Regular moderate coffee consumption is linked to lower risk of Parkinson’s disease and type 2 diabetes.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Caffeine raises dopamine and serotonin levels, which may enhance mood.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The added sugar can contribute to higher blood glucose levels and tooth decay.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee may irritate the stomach in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine can amplify the effects of certain stimulants and reduce the efficacy of sedatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dissolve 1‑2 teaspoons of the product in hot water (80‑90 °C) or add to milk, smoothies, or desserts. It can be used as a base for latte, cappuccino, or cold coffee drinks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct light. After opening, use within 3‑4 weeks to maintain aroma and freshness.

content.title: About
content.content: The Ham Biscuit Sandwich is a quick snack consisting of a slice of ham placed between two dry biscuit crackers. It is often served in school cafeterias and as a light lunch option.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A similar product first appeared in the United States in the 1950s as part of military rations.
The biscuits used are usually unsweetened, making the sandwich less sweet than typical deli sandwiches.
The ham is often smoked, giving the sandwich a distinctive aroma and extending shelf life.
The sandwich is easy to pack in individual portions, popular at buffets and catering events.
In some regions it is served with mustard or mayonnaise to boost flavor.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Ham provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Ham is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of ham and biscuits offers a quick source of calories useful during increased physical activity.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham supplies thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, supporting carbohydrate metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Convenient and portable
items.content: No heating is required, making it practical for travel and on‑the‑go consumption.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ham is often salty, so individuals with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Some ham varieties contain additives that may be undesirable with frequent consumption.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The biscuits may contain wheat, which is important for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The meat‑and‑biscuit combo can be calorie‑rich; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: After opening, keep the sandwich refrigerated and consume within 2‑3 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich can be eaten straight from the pack, cut into bite‑size pieces for children, or topped with mustard, mayonnaise, or fresh vegetables for added flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C in the original packaging. After opening, seal tightly or transfer to an airtight container. Do not keep for more than 5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: The ham salad sandwich on wheat is a classic light lunch or snack. A layer of tender boiled ham, fresh lettuce, tomato and a light mayo‑based dressing is placed between two slices of whole‑grain wheat bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat bread provides slow‑release carbohydrates, helping maintain steady energy levels.
The ham used is often made from pork without added nitrites, making it a more natural option.
The salad component usually includes leaf lettuce and may add cucumber or radish for crunch.
Sandwiches became popular in the United States in the early 20th century with the rise of industrial bakeries.
The combination of ham and mayo offers a good balance of protein and fat.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Ham supplies high‑quality animal protein needed for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Whole‑grain wheat bread
items.content: Whole‑grain wheat bread provides dietary fiber, B‑vitamins and minerals that aid digestion.

items.title: Fresh vegetables
items.content: Lettuce and tomato add vitamin C, potassium and antioxidants.

items.title: Balanced energy
items.content: The mix of carbs, protein and fat delivers sustained satiety.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ham can be high in salt; people monitoring sodium intake should limit portion size.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Some hams contain nitrites, which are undesirable in large amounts.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose a gluten‑free bread.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The sandwich can be calorie‑rich due to mayo and bread fat; control serving size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, preferably cut in half. Add mustard, horseradish or avocado for flavor variation. For a lighter option, replace mayo with a yogurt‑based sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. If the bread begins to dry, wrap it in cling film. Do not keep longer than 2 days to avoid ham spoilage.

content.title: About
content.content: Rum and cola is a popular mixed drink made from light or dark rum combined with cola. The beverage offers a sweet, slightly spicy flavor where the rum’s aroma complements the caramel‑vanilla notes of the soda.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The “Rum & Coke” cocktail originated in the United States in the early 1920s and quickly became a favorite among young people.
There are many variations: with lime (Rum & Coke with Lime), with mint (Mojito‑style), or spiced (Spiced Rum Coke).
In some countries it is considered a “classic” way to serve rum, replacing more elaborate cocktails.
Alcohol content in the finished drink usually ranges from 4‑7 % depending on the ratio.
Rum & Coke is often served in tall glasses over ice with a wedge of lime.

items.title: Moderate consumption may promote relaxation
items.content: Small amounts of alcohol have a calming effect, helping to reduce stress.

items.title: Contains antioxidants from cola
items.content: Caffeine and certain flavor compounds in cola possess antioxidant properties.

items.title: Quick energy boost from sugar
items.content: The sugar in cola raises blood glucose rapidly, providing a short‑term energy surge.

items.title: Alcohol‑related risk
items.content: Excessive intake can lead to intoxication, liver problems, and dependence.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Cola’s sugar contributes to cavities, weight gain, and glucose metabolism issues.

items.title: Caffeine
items.content: Caffeine may cause insomnia, rapid heartbeat, and increased anxiety.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of certain drugs, such as sedatives.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Pour 40‑50 ml of rum into a glass filled with ice, top up with cola, give a gentle stir, and garnish with a lime or lemon wedge. Ratios can be adjusted to taste, but the classic mix is 1 part rum to 3‑4 parts cola.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store rum in a cool, dark place with the bottle tightly sealed. Keep opened cola refrigerated to maintain freshness and carbonation.

content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑sodium spaghetti sauce is a ready‑to‑use tomato‑based sauce seasoned with herbs and spices, containing only 0.3 g of salt per 100 g. It delivers the classic rich flavor of traditional pasta sauce while being suitable for those watching their sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sauce is made from 100 % natural tomatoes with no artificial colors or preservatives.
Salt reduction is achieved by enhancing flavor with basil, oregano and a touch of sugar.
Each batch is tested to ensure the sodium level does not exceed 0.3 g per 100 g.
Tomatoes provide lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
The product is vegetarian and gluten‑free.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Reduced salt helps maintain normal blood pressure and reduces kidney strain.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene has antioxidant properties that support heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The sauce supplies vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium, which aid immune function and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Tomatoes are a source of dietary fiber that promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: One tablespoon provides about 15 kcal, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to tomatoes or the herbs used in the sauce.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: A small amount of sugar is added for balance; people with diabetes should account for it in their carbohydrate budget.

items.title: Acidic ingredients
items.content: The sauce contains citric acid, which can cause mild stomach irritation in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add the sauce to cooked spaghetti, other pasta, lasagna, or use it as a base for casseroles. It also works well as a dip for vegetables or as a flavorful dressing for salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep it refrigerated at 0 °C‑4 °C and consume within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as texture may change.
